idiom_name: struct/class with methods (mutating for value types); extensions for conformance and shared behaviour
implementation_notes: Swift types are the concept: structures hold data and declare behaviour with instance methods (mutating when the value type changes itself), classes hold shared identity, and access control (private, fileprivate, internal) draws the boundary. Extensions add conformance or default behaviour without reopening the declaration, and protocol extensions are the documented way to give every conforming type the shared behaviour; because extensions cannot add stored properties, a concept that needs extra state belongs in the type, not in an extension.
pitfalls: Extensions cannot add stored properties, so 'state' hidden in an extension is recomputed or cached elsewhere - usually the sign the concept belongs in the type.
Value semantics make identity subtle: two equal invoices are the same value, so identity-bearing concepts need a class or an explicit id.
Access control is file-scoped: splitting one concept across files forces fileprivate/internal widening or the split does not compile.
